column1: # Cases a conversational voice meets on the telephone, and what it should say.
# Every expected column here was written by reading the sentence aloud and
# writing down what came out. None of it was generated by Sayso and then
# blessed, which is the only way a test set can find a grammar wrong rather than
# agree with it. Where Sayso and this file disagree, the README's failure-case
# section lists the row and says which of the two is wrong.
# Rows are scored with --style phone, the product setting, except those whose
# note begins "[plain]", which are scored with --style plain. The two styles
# disagree on purpose and both readings have to be right.
# Capitalisation follows Sayso's convention: a proper noun keeps its capital and
# an expansion inherits one when it has become part of a name ("Reading Road",
# "Doctor Lee") and not otherwise ("fifth avenue"). Nothing downstream depends
# on case, but the demo sentence in the pipeline contract does.
# The class column is the class the row is *about*, not necessarily the one that
# wins the span. Rows testing that a class stays out of a span are filed under
# the class that should have been tempted.
